note: Nói ngay — short spontaneous prompts. Row: [id, category, cefr, task, cluster, prompt]
items: Describe what a perfect weekend morning looks like for you.
Talk about your favourite room at home and what you usually do there.
Which kind of weather do you enjoy most, and how does it change your mood?
Tell me about something small that made you smile recently.
Explain how you would build a new daily habit and keep it for a whole month.
Compare your weekdays and your weekends. Which one feels more like the real you?
Should people keep their phones out of the bedroom at night? Explain your view.
Which household chore do you mind the least, and which one do you always put off?
Your room has become very messy and you have only one hour. How would you tackle it?
Talk about one change to your daily routine that made a real difference.
Is it better to be an early riser or a night owl? Consider what each one gains and loses.
Why do small daily rituals, like a cup of tea or a short walk, matter so much to some people?
Would you be happier owning half of what you own now? Defend your answer.
Why do so many people feel busy all the time, even when they are not doing much?
Some people find freedom in strict routines, others in spontaneity. Where do you stand, and why?
Is boredom something to avoid, or can it actually be useful? Explain your thinking.
Describe a friend you enjoy spending time with and what you usually do together.
Talk about something your family likes to do together.
Tell me about a gift you gave someone that made them happy.
Would you lend your things, like books or tools, to people you do not know well? Why?
What makes someone a good listener? Explain with an example you have seen.
Compare making friends at school with making friends online.
A friend is always late when you meet. How would you talk to them about it?
Is it harder to say sorry or to say thank you? Explain your answer.
Describe someone whose advice you often ask for, and why you trust them.
Do you prefer calling people or sending messages? Explain when each one works better.
Why do some friendships fade over time, even without any argument?
When a friend asks for your honest opinion, is it better to be completely honest or to be kind?
What can younger and older generations learn from each other?
Is it better to have a few close friends or many casual ones? Defend your choice.
How far should loyalty to a friend go? Is there a point where it should stop?
Why do people so often misunderstand each other's written messages, and what could reduce this?
Tell me about a game you loved playing as a child.
Talk about a first day you remember well, such as a first day at a new school or job.
Tell the story of a time you lost something and what happened next.
Describe a birthday or celebration that you still remember.
Tell a story about a plan that went wrong but ended well.
Talk about a moment when you felt proud of yourself.
Describe a time you changed your mind about someone after getting to know them.
Tell me about a time a stranger helped you, or you helped a stranger.
Is there a smell or a song that instantly takes you back to the past? Tell me about it.
Tell the story of a day that turned out completely different from what you expected.
Talk about a mistake that taught you more than any lesson at school.
What is something you believed as a child that you now see differently?
Describe a time you had to be braver than you felt.
If you could relive one ordinary day from your past, which would you choose and why?
How reliable are our memories? Talk about a time you remembered something differently from others.
Is nostalgia a healthy feeling, or does it stop us from enjoying the present?
What was your favourite subject at school, and why did you like it?
Describe the place where you study best.
Talk about a teacher you remember and something they did well.
Do you think students should get homework every day? Why or why not?
Explain how you learned a skill outside school, step by step.
Compare learning in a classroom with learning online. Which suits you better?
You have three exams in one week. How would you plan your time?
Do you learn more working alone or in a group? Explain with examples.
Why are you learning English, and how do you hope to use it in the future?
Talk about something you found difficult to learn at first but later understood.
Should schools stop giving grades? Argue for one side.
Why do we forget so much of what we study, and what could help us remember more?
Should schools teach more practical life skills, even if that means less time for academic subjects?
How do you think schools will look different in twenty years?
Can a person learn well without ever failing? Explain your reasoning.
What is the difference between being knowledgeable and being curious, and which matters more?
Describe a job you would like to try for one day.
Would you like to work from home? Say why or why not.
Talk about a job that you think is very useful to society.
Tell me about the first time you earned or saved some money.
What makes a good manager? Explain the qualities you think matter most.
Compare working for a big company with working for a small one.
Your team is going to miss an important deadline. What would you do first?
Would you choose a job you love with a low salary or a job you dislike with a high salary?
Explain how you decide what to do first when you have too many tasks.
Talk about a time you worked in a team. What role did you play?
Is it wiser to take a stable job or to start your own business when you are young?
Which jobs do you think will become more important in the next twenty years, and why?
Why do some people feel exhausted by work even when they like their job?
Should companies move to a four-day working week? Make a case for your view.
Is leadership something people are born with, or something they learn? Explain.
What makes work feel meaningful, and is it the employer's job to provide that meaning?
What do you do when you need to relax after a difficult day?
Talk about one goal you have for this year.
Where do you feel most confident, and why?
Tell me about a time you felt nervous and how you handled it.
What do you do when you lose motivation halfway through something?
Talk about a small risk you took that you are glad you took.
How do you make a decision when two choices seem equally good?
How do you usually react to criticism, and how would you like to react?
Is it important to leave your comfort zone regularly? Why?
Why do people put off tasks they know are important?
Is aiming for perfection a strength or a weakness? Consider both sides.
Should people share their failures as openly as their successes? Defend your view.
What advice would you give your younger self, and why that advice?
Why do people compare themselves with others so often, and is it ever helpful?
How much of success comes from luck and how much from effort? Explain your view.
Can chasing happiness actually make people less happy? Explain your thinking.
Talk about a film you enjoyed and why you would recommend it.
Describe a book or story you loved when you were younger.
Do you like listening to music while you work or study? Why?
Talk about something creative you like to do, even if you are not an expert.
What makes a story really good? Explain using a story you know.
Is it better to read the book or watch the film first? Explain your choice.
If you could master one art form overnight, which would it be and what would you create?
Would you rather spend an afternoon in a museum or at a concert? Explain.
Describe a fictional character you would like to meet in real life.
Explain how people can be creative in ordinary jobs, not only in the arts.
Why do film studios keep remaking old films, and is that good for audiences?
Should art and music be as important as maths at school? Argue your case.
Why do people watch whole series in one weekend, and what do they miss by doing so?
Do limits, such as little time or few materials, make people more or less creative?
Who decides what counts as art: the artist, the audience, or the experts?
How might storytelling change in the future, and what about it will stay the same?
Talk about an app you use every day and how it helps you.
Could you spend a whole day without your phone? Explain why or why not.
Describe a device at home that makes your life easier.
Tell me about a time you taught someone how to use a new device or app.
Do people enjoy special moments less when they spend them taking photos? Explain.
Why do people post about their lives on social media?
How would you help a younger relative spend less time on screens?
Do you prefer shopping online or in a shop? Explain your reasons.
Which invention from the last fifty years has changed daily life the most?
Should apps be allowed to send notifications late at night? Explain your view.
How has constant access to the internet changed the way people concentrate?
Would you share more personal data in exchange for more convenient services? Where would you draw the line?
At what age should children get their own smartphone? Defend your answer.
Why have online creators become so influential, and is that a good thing?
Should we let recommendation systems decide what news and entertainment we see? Explain the risks and benefits.
How might homes change when robots can do most household jobs?
What makes a place worth visiting a second time?
Do you prefer holidays by the sea or in the mountains? Why?
How do you usually travel to school or work, and what do you like or dislike about it?
Do you prefer travelling by bus, train or plane? Why?
You are in a foreign city, your phone is dead and you are lost. What would you do?
Is it better to plan every detail of a trip or to leave room for surprises?
What do you always take on a trip, and what have you learned not to bring?
Would you like to travel alone? Explain the advantages and disadvantages.
Tell the story of a travel problem and how it was solved.
What would make more people use public transport in your city?
How does tourism change the lives of people who live in popular places?
Should people fly less to protect the environment, even if it makes travel harder?
Why do people feel the need to travel, when they could learn about places online?
Should young people take a year to travel before university or work? Argue your view.
Does travelling really make people more open-minded? Explain why or why not.
How will people get around cities in thirty years, and what will we have to give up?
Describe a dish from your country that you would recommend to a visitor.
Talk about a festival or holiday you enjoy and how people celebrate it.
Do you prefer cooking at home or eating out? Why?
Tell me about a meal you will never forget.
Explain how to make a simple dish you know well, step by step.
Compare street food with restaurant food. Which tells you more about a place?
Which tradition from your culture would you most like to keep alive, and why?
Talk about a custom from another country that surprised you.
You are cooking for guests with different diets. How would you plan the meal?
Why are family meals important in many cultures?
Why has fast food become so popular around the world, and what has been lost?
Should traditions change with the times, or stay the same to keep their meaning?
Should restaurants be required to give away food they cannot sell? Argue your view.
When cultures mix through travel and the internet, what is gained and what is lost?
What makes a person feel that they belong to a culture?
How might the way we produce and eat food change in the next fifty years?
Which sounds of nature do you enjoy most, and where do you hear them?
If you could be any animal for one day, which would you choose?
What is your favourite season, and what do you like to do then?
Tell me about a day you spent outdoors that you enjoyed.
What small things do you do to reduce waste, and why?
How could your school or workplace use less plastic?
Are zoos good for animals? Explain your opinion.
Do people who live close to nature live better lives? Explain.
Talk about something in nature near you that has changed since you were a child.
Why do some people still drop litter, and how could this change?
Can a country grow its economy and protect the environment at the same time?
Should people eat less meat for environmental reasons? Defend your view.
How do hotter summers change everyday life in cities?
Do individual actions really matter for the environment, or only government action? Explain.
Should rivers, forests or animals have legal rights? Explain the idea and your view.
How might your hometown need to adapt to a changing climate over the next thirty years?
Describe your hometown to someone who has never been there.
Talk about a street or area in your city that you like.
Would you rather live in a big city or a small village? Why?
Which places in your area do people use to meet each other?
If you were in charge of your city for one day, what would you change first?
What makes a neighbourhood feel like a real community?
Should cities protect old buildings or replace them with modern ones?
How important are parks and green spaces in a city? Explain.
What sounds do you hear most where you live, and how do they affect you?
How could people in an apartment building get to know their neighbours better?
Why do so many young people move to big cities, and what do they leave behind?
Should cars be banned from city centres? Consider who benefits and who loses.
What happens to a city when housing becomes too expensive for young people?
Should cities spend money on public art when there are other needs? Argue your view.
Would you accept more cameras and sensors in public places if they made your city safer?
Describe the city you hope to live in thirty years from now, and what would make it possible.
What kind of exercise do you enjoy, or would like to try?
Describe a healthy meal you like to eat.
What do you do when you cannot fall asleep?
Tell me about a sport or game you played that you enjoyed.
What helps you deal with stress during a busy week?
Is it better to exercise in a gym or outdoors? Explain your choice.
How could you encourage your friends or family to move more every day?
Is healthy food too expensive? Explain your view.
Which unhealthy habit do you think is the hardest for people to give up, and why?
Why do many people sit for most of the day, and what problems can that cause?
Do fitness apps and trackers make people healthier, or just more anxious?
Should governments tax sugary drinks? Defend your opinion.
Why is it easier today for people to talk about mental health than in the past?
Why is rest just as important as hard work?
Is staying healthy mainly a personal responsibility or a shared one? Explain.
If people could live to 120 in good health, how would society have to change?
What does it mean to be polite in your culture?
Talk about a way people in your area help others.
Do you sometimes buy things you do not really need? Why do you think that happens?
Describe a person you admire and what they have done.
How do advertisements make people want to buy things?
Do brands matter to you when you buy clothes or devices? Why?
In what ways is life easier today than it was for your grandparents, and in what ways is it harder?
Why do young people follow trends so quickly?
What could encourage people to be kinder to strangers?
Would you like to be famous? Explain the good and bad sides.
Is buying second-hand the future of shopping? Explain the reasons behind your view.
Why do many people feel lonely even though they are more connected than ever?
Should sixteen-year-olds be allowed to vote? Argue for one side.
What does success mean to you, and how is it different from what society expects?
Is it possible for everyone in a society to have truly equal opportunities? Explain.
Why are more people choosing to live alone, and what does that say about modern life?
Would you like to travel to space? Why or why not?
Talk about an experiment or science lesson you remember.
What is something in nature that you find amazing?
Which everyday object would you most like to understand better, and why?
Explain a fact about the world that surprised you when you first learned it.
Should countries spend money on space exploration when there are problems on Earth?
Do scientists and artists think in similar ways? Explain your view.
If you could invent something to solve one everyday problem, what would it be?
Is science fiction useful, or just entertainment? Explain.
How do you decide whether a piece of health or science news is true?
Which scientific discovery do you think changed ordinary people's lives the most?
Is it acceptable to test medicines on animals? Explain the arguments on both sides.
Why do some students lose interest in science, and how could that change?
Will humans ever live on another planet? What would make it worthwhile?
Should there be limits on what scientists are allowed to research? Explain your view.
Why do scientists sometimes change their advice, and should that make us trust them less?
If you could have one superpower for a day, which would you choose and what would you do?
Imagine you have a free day and no money to spend. How would you enjoy it?
If you could speak any language perfectly tomorrow, which one would you choose?
You can take only three things to an island for a month. What do you choose?
If you could visit any time in history for one day, where would you go and why?
You find a wallet with money but no name inside. What do you do?
If you could swap lives with someone for a week, who would it be?
There is no electricity in your town for three days. How would you manage?
If you could add one new rule to your school or workplace, what would it be?
Imagine the internet disappeared for a year. What would change in your life first?
If you could know one fact about your future, would you want to? Explain.
A small town has money for only one project: a library, a sports centre or a park. Which should it choose?
What would a city without money look like? How would people get what they need?
You promised to help a friend, but you get a great opportunity on the same day. What do you do?
What would happen if nobody could tell a lie for a whole year?
If you could erase one bad memory, would you? What might you lose by doing so?
